methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a well-designed nationwide population-based cohort (n=778,943) with high-quality linked Swedish registries (SVEVAC, NVR, PDR, NPR, NCR). HPV vaccination is appropriately handled as a time-varying exposure with delayed entry and attained age as the underlying time scale, mitigating immortal-time bias. Poisson regression is appropriate for incidence rate ratios, and the fully adjusted model includes a comprehensive covariate set with sensitivity analyses using 1- and 2-year buffer periods to address prevalent HPV infection at vaccination. Limitations include lack of pre-specified power calculation (though sample is very large), residual confounding from unmeasured smoking and sexual behavior (acknowledged in the Discussion), potential vaccination-status misclassification (~8% of 2006-2015 doses, acknowledged), and no formal multiplicity correction for subgroup/anatomic-site analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual nationwide retrospective cohort study using registry-linked data, mapping to Oxford LoE 2b. The clinical question (real-world effectiveness of quadrivalent HPV vaccination against high-grade vulvovaginal lesions) is highly relevant because robust evidence on noncervical HPV-related lesions is sparse and directly informs program-level vaccination policy. Findings showing a 55% reduction in high-grade vulvovaginal lesions with vaccination at ages 10-16 and population-level incidence reductions across subsidized/catch-up birth cohorts support ongoing public health recommendations to expand early HPV vaccination. Endpoints are patient-relevant (high-grade precancer and invasive cancer), though invasive-cancer accrual is limited and could not be analyzed separately.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the applicable standard and is explicitly cited by the authors. Key observational-reporting elements are well addressed: study setting, data sources per register, inclusion/exclusion with a flow diagram (Figure 1), time-varying exposure handling, covariate definitions, outcome ICD-10 codes, and sensitivity analyses. Minor omissions include no explicit statement on protocol pre-registration and no formal missing-data imputation beyond a 'missing' category. Data/code availability is weak in the blinded text: Swedish registry data are generally not openly shareable due to privacy law, and no code repository or analytic code sharing statement is present.

novelty_literature.justification: The novelty is primarily empirical and population-level: this is only the second large real-world observational study of HPV vaccination against high-grade vulvovaginal lesions (after the Danish study by Dehlendorff et al., 2021 - reference 8) and the first to leverage the Swedish registry stratified by birth-cohort vaccination program (opportunistic vs subsidized vs catch-up). It extends prior work by quantifying program-level incidence reduction tied to vaccine delivery mode, which is policy-relevant. However, the central finding (vaccine effectiveness, stronger protection with vaccination before 17) replicates the Danish cohort and the Xu et al. systematic review of trials, so this is a meaningful extension rather than a conceptually novel contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written and well organized following standard IMRaD structure, with the abstract accurately reflecting the quantitative findings (IRR 0.63, 95% CI 0.50-0.81) and acronyms expanded on first use. The methods section is detailed and transparent about the time-varying exposure, delayed-entry framework, and covariate construction. The discussion appropriately contrasts with the Danish cohort and the Xu et al. systematic review, and candidly enumerates seven limitations including residual confounding, misclassification, and causal interpretation. Figure/table captions in the blinded text are terse and stand alone; the Figure 2 caption gives a helpful worked example of the time-varying contribution.

key_strengths: Nationwide Swedish registry cohort of 778,943 women with comprehensive linkage across SVEVAC, NVR, PDR, NPR, and NCR provides high statistical power and generalizability
Rigorous handling of HPV vaccination as a time-varying exposure with delayed entry and attained age as time scale, avoiding immortal-time bias
Sensitivity analyses with 1- and 2-year buffer periods strengthen causal inference by excluding prevalent HPV infection at vaccination
Novel policy-relevant stratification by birth cohort tied to opportunistic, subsidized, and catch-up vaccination programs quantifies real-world program effects
Transparent, thorough enumeration of seven limitations including residual confounding and vaccination-status misclassification
key_concerns: Replicates prior Danish cohort findings (Dehlendorff et al., 2021) and systematic-review evidence, limiting conceptual novelty to the program-level/birth-cohort analysis
No pre-registered protocol or multiplicity correction for the multiple subgroup and anatomic-site analyses
Residual confounding by smoking, sexual behavior, and screening participation cannot be excluded; parental SES is only a partial proxy
Low number of invasive cancer events precludes separate assessment of vaccine effectiveness against invasive vulvar/vaginal cancer
Data and analytic-code availability is not demonstrated in the blinded text, limiting reproducibility
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a methodologically rigorous, large-scale population-based cohort study with policy-relevant findings on quadrivalent HPV vaccination and noncervical lesions, suitable for a top-tier oncology/clinical journal (Tier 1) with minor revisions to clarify multiplicity handling, data/code availability, and the incremental novelty relative to the Danish cohort.
